ctx.x: Yeah, in fact, people had bought tickets for the Frank Foster concert and after…. End of CD #4
Sweets, you were just telling us about the tour to Japan with the band that you and Frank Wess co-led and had many Basie-ites in it.

items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Most critics say that the greatest soloists were with the Old Testament band, the Lester Youngs, the Buck Claytons, Harry Edison...

ctx.x: We can add him if you’d like. And Marshall Royal himself. All excellent soloists but most critics say that the greatest soloists were with the Old Testament band, the Lester Youngs, the Buck Claytons, Harry Edison, Earle Warren, Jack Washington on baritone and saxophone, Buddy Tate, Don Byas, even Illinois Jacquet, who was with the Basie band for a minute. Most critics seemed to favor the old soloists, the Old Testament band.
What do you think about that judgment?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Frank Foster is a good writer.

ctx.x: And Frank Wess was a good writer, Frank Foster is a good writer.
Which one -- Frank Foster did "Every Day," didn't he? I think.
